lines: In Workforce, open Resource costs, then select Add resource profile.
Choose Unit as the Subject type and select the fictional community van.
Give the profile a clear Name and check its Effective and Expires dates.
The saved example covers October through November and uses U S D.
A resource profile prices the selected unit, asset or external resource class.
Check that subject before applying rates to an operational resource.
In Depreciation, the example enters an Acquisition cost of ten thousand
and a Salvage value of one thousand.
Choose Per operating hour as the Allocation basis and enter
nine hundred Useful life units.
The form gives the straight-line formula: cost minus salvage, divided by life.
These fictional inputs produce ten per operating hour.
Expected annual utilization is six hundred.
Use units that match the chosen basis; this software example does
not prescribe an accounting policy.
Add a Cost components row for Fuel or energy.
Use the operating-hour basis, Consumption of two and Unit price
of four, with Manual as the Source.
That combination produces eight per operating hour.
Mark the fictional component and profile Approved, then select Save.
The saved profile row shows depreciation of ten and one component.
Reopening lets you check the subject, dates, approval and component inputs
instead of relying on an unsaved form.
Open Work entries and add the fictional worker’s two Regular
hours on November second.
Enter the exercise call number, fifty-one thousand and one, in Call number.
Keep the chosen establishment, identify the fictional source,
and review Approved before Save.
The saved row shows two hours, the call context and Yes.
Associating hours with the correct call is essential: an approved work
entry without that call relationship would not be the same call-cost input.
Open Cost runs and find Call number with Calculate call cost.
This control uses work entries and resource usage recorded against
that call and supplies no revenue.
The recording retains a before-and-after comparison from this exercise.
Its first successful result shows fifty-four in Personnel, zero in
Resources and fifty-four total.
Two hours at the configured loaded estimate of twenty-seven
explain the personnel amount.
A zero resource result does not prove the vehicle cost nothing; first
check whether usage was recorded.
From the cost result, open Resource usage and add a reading.
Select the same community van, the exercise date, Incident as the
Phase and Manual as the Source.
Enter two Operating hours, then review Approved and Save.
The saved usage row confirms two operating hours.
This exercise uses operating hours, so it leaves odometer, engine-hour
and fuel-quantity inputs empty.
Match the recorded measurement to the allocation basis rather
than entering the same work into several unrelated meter fields.
Recalculate the call after saving its usage.
The recorded result now shows Personnel of fifty-four, Resources
of thirty-six and a total of ninety.
The resource contribution is twenty in depreciation plus
sixteen in fuel or energy: two hours multiplied by ten and eight.
Compare the input quantities and saved result together.
A configured resource profile needs corresponding usage before this
example contributes a resource amount.
Return to the same work entry and enter forty in Approved payroll cost,
retaining a clearly fictional source.
Save and verify forty on the work-entry row, then recalculate.
Personnel becomes forty, Resources stays thirty-six and
the total becomes seventy-six.
The form explains that this approved payroll input replaces the estimate.
No payroll system was contacted.
The saved result still has one Missing input and is not Frozen;
its index says Needs review.
Inspect that state before using a total as a finished cost report.
These controls can support security patrols, search and rescue, wildland
contractors, industrial emergency teams, community paramedicine or mental health
response, and fire or E M S operations.
Use a resource, measurement basis and call context that fit your organization.
Verify saved inputs, recalculate after changes, and resolve review
items before relying on the result.
All amounts here are fictional software inputs, with no external payment,
invoice or real payroll import.
